windowTitle: Serial integration stage 5 - default OPL App reservation carries no CapabilityVersion
scope: Prove, against Serve's real owner store, that the default OPL App is a first-class delivery source: Reserve accepts an explicit opl_app selection backed by an approved Runtime Release with no Package/Build/CapabilityVersion, and refuses a mixed selection that also names a CapabilityVersion. No production source, contract, schema, migration or generator changed.
implemented: services/serve/internal/delivery/write_postgres_test.go: TestServeDefaultAppReservationCarriesNoCapabilityVersion drives Serve.Reserve over a real RuntimeControlProductService client surface (runtimeControlForServe) with a Runtime Release whose PublisherContract carries the immutable OCI and application revision template; it asserts the persisted serve.agent_deployments row is application_kind='opl_app' with empty capability_version_id and the selected runtime_version_id, that exactly one Runtime Release reference claim is acquired, and that a mixed source naming CapabilityVersionId is rejected with InvalidArgument.

The default App deployment descriptor is the release's own publisher contract (DEPLOYMENT_DESCRIPTOR_PROVENANCE_ENUM_RUNTIME_RELEASE), never a caller-supplied image, matching the Reserve admission in services/serve/internal/delivery/write.go.

verification.environment: local loopback PostgreSQL container for the owner-migration tests
cases: TestServeDefaultAppReservationCarriesNoCapabilityVersion: default App reservation persists application_kind=opl_app, capability_version_id empty, runtime_version_id=rv-opl-app, acquires 1 Runtime Release claim, and a mixed CapabilityVersionId source is InvalidArgument.
All existing Serve delivery and migration suites still pass.

notRun: No real Runtime Control, TKE cluster, Candidate build, Instance deployment or production readback; this is a Cloud source-level proof of the default OPL App first-delivery path.
The publisher opl-model-config/v1 apply/readback, Serve's own TKE application-execution writer (I06), the real configured RouteProvider and Deploy-to-Fence/Activate orchestration (I07) remain open.
claimBoundary: This receipt claims a Cloud source-level correctness proof with a focused isolated-PostgreSQL test: Serve reserves the default OPL App from an approved Runtime Release without a CapabilityVersion and rejects the mixed source. It does not claim the full two-combo end-to-end chain, a Candidate, deployment or production acceptance.
